text:
alex: Quick question on gateway matching precedence — want to lock this before I wire up rollout UI. Thoughts?

marta: TL;DR: prefer deterministic order: host exact > host wildcard > path exact > longest-prefix > header matches > service fallback. Keeps stable behavior.

sam: Agree but need to clarify header-based overrides: should header match outrank path prefix? e.g., tenant-specific routes

alex: Example: tenant header routes for beta customers should override generic /v1/* handlers.

ying: I think header matches are orthogonal — treat them as additional selectors that must match; tie-breakers still by specificity. so header doesn't 'outrank' path but narrows candidates.

alex: Proposed precedence algorithm:
1) Filter by host match (exact then wildcard)
2) Within same host specificity, filter by path specificity (exact > longest prefix)
3) From remaining, require header selectors to match (more header key/value pairs = more specific)
4) If still ambiguous, pick route with explicit service mapping; otherwise fail/fallback to default-backend

sam: Sounds good. A couple edge cases:
- two routes same host+path, one has header x-tenant=acme, other has x-tenant present (any value). Which is more specific? exact value > presence > absent.
- path params: /v1/users/:id vs /v1/users (exact). exact wins.

marta: Also need to surface this in Console: show the matched rule in trace and explain why it won. Tracing header+host+path score.

dev-console: +1. UX note: show computed "score" and the criterias used. Also helpful for rollouts to highlight which routes are eligible for canary.

alex: Quick config sketch:
```yaml
routes:
  - host: api.redwood.com
    path: /v1/embeddings
    service: embeddings-v2
  - host: *.redwood.com
    path_prefix: /v1
    service: frontend-proxy
  - host: api.redwood.com
    path_prefix: /v1
    headers:
      x-tenant: acme
    service: embeddings-v2-acme
```

ying: One more: precedence with rewrites/overrides — if a route rewrites path then matching must be before rewrite. i.e. matching uses original request values; rewrite only transforms for upstream.

sam: Agreed. Also quotas: quota keys should derive from the winning route and include header-derived tenant id if present.

marta: I'll add this to the design doc and include example traces. Also propose small unit tests for ambiguous sets.

deploy-bot: Deployed routing matcher v0.3 to staging — see /deploys/1719933400 :rocket:

alex: Great. I'll implement matcher order in `gateway/matcher.go` and add Console display hooks. Thanks :thumbsup:

ying: I'll add e2e for rewrite and header precedence. ping me if you need test fixtures.

sam: leaving note — update docs and changelog for 1. API matching precedence 2. header specificity ranking

marta: ok. moving to PR review queue.
